This guide covers ten medical coding companies in California that provide medical coding services to healthcare organizations through autonomous AI platforms, hybrid automation with medical coding specialists, or outsourced medical coding teams.

## 1. CombineHealth


CombineHealth is a **self-learning autonomous medical coding software that helps California healthcare providers automate their coding workflows.** The software reads completed clinical encounter documentation directly from the EHR and returns billing-ready codes without manual intervention on routine charts.


CombineHealth **covers**[ICD-10-CM](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/icd-10-explained-a-comprehensive-guide-to-medical-coding) **,**[CPT,](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/cpt-codes-what-are-they-types-and-uses) **HCPCS Level II,**[E/M levels](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/e-m-coding-guide) **,**[modifiers](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/modifiers-in-medical-billing) **, and provider attribution** across professional and facility settings. It also evaluates coding decisions against downstream claim outcomes to build payer-specific coding intelligence over time.


Across customer deployments, CombineHealth delivers:


- 97.2%+ medical coding accuracy
- Up to 85% coding automation
- Up to 75% fewer coding-related denials
- 5× more CDI opportunities identified
- Up to 4% more captured revenue
- Under 12-hour turnaround in large emergency medicine deployments


### Feature #1: Payer-Aware Autonomous Medical Coding


CombineHealth **applies configured payer rules, coverage policies, and contract requirements** during the initial medical coding pass. For California healthcare organizations managing Medi-Cal, commercial, and Medicare Advantage payers, this helps ensure coding decisions account for payer-specific requirements before claims reach the payer.


> **Recommended read:**[Autonomous Medical Coding in 2026: A Complete Guide](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/autonomous-medical-coding-guide)


### Feature #2: Explainable Code-Level Rationale


**Each medical code includes the clinical evidence supporting it,** the guideline or payer rule applied, and its confidence level. Medical coders and auditors can review this rationale within their existing workflow, creating an audit trail for OIG reviews, payer audits, and internal compliance programs.


> **Recommended read** :[Explainability in AI for Healthcare RCM](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/explainability-in-ai-for-healthcare-rcm)


### Feature #3: Complete-Encounter Documentation Validation


CombineHealth **reads the full clinical note, rather than only a charge summary or structured extract, to validate each code.** It identifies diagnosis-to-procedure linkage gaps, specificity shortfalls, and unsupported modifiers, then surfaces them as CDI opportunities before the claim moves to billing.


### Feature #4: Coding Automation at Scale


CombineHealth **autonomously codes most charts without human intervention, supporting high-volume environments while maintaining accuracy and turnaround** . It is designed to handle volume spikes consistently, allowing health systems and[RCM organizations](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/healthcare-revenue-cycle-management-software-companies) to scale coding without creating operational bottlenecks.


### Case Study: CombineHealth Sustained 98%+ Accuracy at High Volume Emergency Coding


Brault, a 40-plus-year emergency medicine RCM organization, deployed CombineHealth after a previous autonomous coding vendor couldn't sustain accuracy in production. CombineHealth **held 98%+ accuracy across CPT, E/M, ICD, modifiers, and CDI** in recurring production audits, maintained sub-12-hour turnaround through 2–3× volume spikes, and cut new-site go-live from roughly six weeks to about two weeks.


[Read the Case Study](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/brault-autonomous-coding)


### Case Study: CombineHealth Identified 5× More CDI Gaps Than Human Coders


In a 1,000-chart parallel coding study, **CombineHealth coded emergency department charts alongside expert human coders, matching them at 98%+ accuracy,** cutting coding turnaround by approximately 50%, and identifying 5× more clinical documentation gaps than the human-only workflow.


[Read the Case Study](https://www.combinehealth.ai/resources/customer-success-stories/case-study/ai-matched-expert-coders)


**Best for:** Physician groups, RCM organizations, and hospitals that need configurable automation across a mixed California payer environment.


## 2. Fathom


Fathom, headquartered in San Francisco, delivers fully autonomous professional and facility coding across multiple specialties at the same time. This removes the department-by-department rollout that can slow deployment with other vendors.


Its multi-specialty deployment model lets California health systems go live across departments at once instead of specialty by specialty. Fathom is listed in Epic's Toolbox for fully autonomous coding and is expanding into inpatient DRG facility coding with academic medical center partners.


**Key features:**


- Multi-specialty simultaneous deployment across professional and facility coding workflows
- Epic Toolbox designation for fully autonomous coding, with integrations with Cerner, athenahealth, MEDITECH, and eClinicalWorks
- Expanding inpatient DRG coding capability in development with large academic health systems


**Best for:** Large California health systems and RCM organizations seeking enterprise-scale autonomous coding across multiple specialties and departments at once.


## 3. CodaMetrix


CodaMetrix is an autonomous medical coding platform developed within Mass General Brigham and now deployed across a large network of Epic health systems nationally. It is designed for complex academic and enterprise environments where coding based on a single encounter may not provide enough clinical context.


Its key differentiator is longitudinal patient record ingestion, pulling data from problem lists, lab results, imaging reports, and prior visit notes. This provides more clinical context for complex diagnoses such as sepsis, heart failure, and CKD, where severity staging can depend on clinical trends rather than a single visit note.


**Key features:**


- Autonomous coding across radiology, pathology, endoscopy, surgery, ED, and E&M
- Longitudinal record ingestion for higher diagnostic specificity in complex, multi-visit cases
- Direct charge router write-back through HL7 and FHIR with Epic, GE, MEDITECH, and Cerner


**Best for:** Large California health systems and academic medical centers on Epic or Cerner that need multi-specialty autonomous coding with deep longitudinal patient context.


## 4. Nym Health


Nym Health's coding engine uses Clinical Language Understanding (CLU) architecture to read the full clinical document rather than matching keywords or extracting structured fields. This creates a complete, auditable trace behind each code assignment, supporting internal compliance reviews and external payer audits.


Nym operates with zero human intervention on its primary coding path, holding ambiguous charts instead of coding them at low confidence. The platform is SOC 2 Type II certified and has live deployments at Ochsner Health, Geisinger, and Inova.


**Key features:**


- Six supported specialties: emergency medicine, radiology, outpatient surgery, outpatient visits, inpatient professional services, and urgent care
- Full code-level audit trail with SOC 2 Type II certification
- Integrates with Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, and MEDITECH, with typical go-live in 60–90 days


**Best for:** California hospitals and physician groups in Nym's supported specialties that need fully autonomous coding with a traceable decision trail and a published implementation timeline.


## 5. AGS Health


AGS Health combines AI-assisted autonomous coding with AAPC- and AHIMA-certified medical coders, running both in parallel. High-volume routine encounters move through automation, while complex or payer-sensitive cases go to coding specialists for review and finalization.


This hybrid model suits California organizations moving from fully outsourced medical coding to a technology-led approach without replacing their existing coding team. It also works for specialties with variable case complexity, such as oncology, behavioral health, and complex surgery, where pure automation may not yet reach target rates.


**Key features:**


- Hybrid delivery combining AI autonomous coding with certified coder oversight for complex cases
- Inpatient and outpatient coding, CDI, coding audits, and denial prevention
- EHR integrations across Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, MEDITECH, eClinicalWorks, and Allscripts


**Best for:** California hospitals and multispecialty groups that need certified coding expertise alongside automation, particularly for specialties with variable and complex case mix.


## 6. CorroHealth


CorroHealth frames its offering as "clinical revenue integrity," combining medical coding execution with clinical documentation improvement and audit programs rather than treating coding as a standalone function.


For California hospitals where coding errors may stem from provider documentation habits rather than coder error alone, CorroHealth's consulting arm addresses these issues across the organization instead of correcting individual charts.


**Key features:**


- Autonomous coding technology combined with facility and professional coding personnel
- CDI integrated with coding workflows, with audit programs targeting upstream documentation gaps
- Charge capture support and revenue integrity consulting across inpatient and outpatient settings


**Best for:** California hospital systems that need coding and CDI improvement together, particularly where provider documentation patterns are a major source of coding inaccuracy.


## 7. GeBBS Healthcare Solutions


GeBBS Healthcare Solutions is headquartered in Los Angeles, making it one of the few companies on this list with a California base. It combines agentic AI with AHIMA- and AAPC-certified medical coders, routing standard encounters through automation while keeping certified coders involved in complex cases.


GeBBS serves a broad range of California providers, including FQHCs, community hospitals, and large integrated health systems. It is also recognized as a leader in outsourced coding by Everest Group and Modern Healthcare's Top Largest RCM Firms.


**Key features:**


- Large certified coder bench covering inpatient, outpatient, professional coding, risk adjustment, and CDI
- Agentic AI combined with certified human oversight across the coding workflow
- Compatible with Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, GE Centricity, NextGen, and additional platforms


**Best for:** California providers, including FQHCs, community hospitals, and integrated health systems, that want to scale coding without building internal headcount and prefer a California-headquartered outsourcing partner.


## 8. Omega Healthcare


Omega Healthcare is a technology-enabled healthcare management services company and an IDC MarketScape leader for U.S. Revenue Cycle Management. Its Omega Digital Platform combines AI, machine learning, RPA, NLP, and predictive analytics across RCM workflows, including denial prediction, claims routing, and coding.


Its medical coding services include HCC risk adjustment, professional and facility coding, and chart audits. Omega's large global workforce allows it to support California health systems and payer organizations that need coding capacity across multiple service lines at the same time.


**Key features:**


- HCC risk adjustment, professional and facility coding, and chart audits on one platform
- AI-enhanced workflows with Epic-specific automations and real-time analytics
- Large global workforce supporting high-volume, multi-service-line coding operations


**Best for:** Large California health systems and payer organizations that need AI-enhanced coding operations at enterprise scale across multiple service lines.


## 9. MedKoder


MedKoder uses 100% US-based certified coders across professional and facility service lines. Its Complete Coding Automation platform combines AI coding suggestions with expert human review on every chart before results reach billing. Unlike fully autonomous platforms, a credentialed auditor finalizes every output.


MedKoder also provides standalone audit and education services, allowing organizations to engage it for compliance audits, CDI consulting, or provider education without committing to full-volume outsourcing. There is no minimum volume requirement.


**Key features:**


- 100% US-based certified coders across inpatient, outpatient, professional, and facility coding
- AI coding suggestions reviewed and finalized by expert human auditors on every chart
- Standalone audit, CDI, DRG oversight, HCC risk adjustment, and provider education programs


**Best for:** California physician groups, community hospitals, and FQHCs that need US-based coding staff, project-based audit services, or flexible outsourcing without volume minimums.


## 10. Solventum


Solventum's 360 Encompass System, built on decades of 3M Health Information Systems coding work, is a computer-assisted coding and CDI platform used across U.S. hospital systems.


Solventum has added an autonomous coding module that qualifies specific encounters for touchless processing, while other encounters continue through standard CAC review. Computer-assisted coding accelerates coder review but does not replace it on most charts. Autonomous processing applies only to qualifying encounters and is not the default mode.


**Key features:**


- Computer-assisted coding for facility and professional workflows with strong inpatient DRG capture
- Autonomous coding module for qualifying encounters within the standard CAC workflow
- Available as cloud SaaS or on-premises, with CDI and real-time clinical intelligence reporting


**Best for:** California hospital systems running Solventum or 3M tools, or organizations that prioritize inpatient DRG accuracy and integrated CDI over fully autonomous outpatient coding.


## How We Evaluated the Medical Coding Companies


Each company was assesse **d** **against criteria specific to medical coding** , not general RCM services where medical coding is bundled but not the main focus.


We **clearly distinguished between fully autonomous coding, computer-assisted coding, and outsourced coding with AI assistance** because each model has different staffing, turnaround, and denial implications.


We reviewed audit capabilities,[explainable code-level rationale](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/explainability-in-ai-medical-coding) , EHR integration depth, supported specialties, CDI capabilities, and the ability to apply Medi-Cal and payer-specific requirements.


For California relevance, we focused on companies with a documented track record of serving organizations with similar payer complexity, including Medi-Cal managed care, commercial HMOs, and Medicare Advantage under CalAIM, regardless of where the company is headquartered.


## What Should California Providers Expect From a Medical Coding Company?


### Medical Coding From the Complete Encounter


The platform should read the full clinical note, not just a charge summary. Coding from incomplete documentation can miss specificity, misrepresent severity, and under-capture diagnoses that affect HCC risk scores and DRG weights.


### Payer-Specific and Medi-Cal Compliance


Medi-Cal managed care plans, CalAIM-linked services, and commercial HMO contracts can have plan-specific requirements. A medical coding company should apply those requirements at the chart level rather than relying on coders to catch payer-specific issues during exception review.


### Audit Capability and Explainable Decisions


California providers operating under Medi-Cal audit programs or OIG focus areas need a defensible record of each coding decision. Treat explainable code-level rationale as a procurement requirement, not an implementation detail.


### EHR Write-Back to Billing Fields


A company that delivers coded results in a report instead of writing them into EHR billing fields shifts manual entry back to staff. Confirm the write-back path during the demo rather than relying only on the statement of work.


## Choose a Medical Coding Company Built for California's Payer Environment


California providers need more than a medical coding vendor that processes claims at volume. They need one that applies Medi-Cal managed care, commercial HMO, and Medicare Advantage requirements at the chart level, without manual reconfiguration every time a plan changes.


The companies in this guide approach that differently—autonomous AI, hybrid automation with specialists, or outsourced coding teams. Evaluate each against your payer mix, EHR environment, and specialty coverage before deciding.

## FAQ


### How is CombineHealth different from other medical coding companies on this list?


CombineHealth is different from other medical coding companies because it goes beyond code generation with a self-learning system that evaluates coding decisions against actual claim outcomes, including denials, reimbursements, and underpayments. It uses these outcomes to build[payer intelligence](https://www.combinehealth.ai/blog/payer-intelligence-ai-medical-coding) and continuously adapt its coding strategy, helping reduce coding-related denials while maintaining coding accuracy.


### Does CombineHealth work inside existing EHR and billing workflows?


Yes. CombineHealth reads completed documentation directly from the source EHR and returns billing-ready codes into existing billing fields, with no separate coding environment, manual re-entry, or workflow changes required for your team.


### Does a medical coding company need to be California-based to apply Medi-Cal rules?


No. What matters is whether the company can configure Medi-Cal managed care requirements at the chart level. A California office is not required if the vendor can support the relevant payer rules and workflows.


### What is the difference between autonomous coding and computer-assisted coding?


Autonomous coding produces billing-ready codes without human review on routine charts and routes exceptions for review. Computer-assisted coding suggests codes for a human coder to review and approve, so the manual step remains part of the workflow.


### How should California providers evaluate coding companies for Medi-Cal managed care?


Ask how the vendor applies plan-specific coding requirements, how quickly it updates rules when payer requirements change, and whether it has documented experience coding for Medi-Cal managed care plans.
